practices.prior_belief: Set client timeouts to avoid hung requests: set serverSelectionTimeoutMS (e.g. 5000 ms) and socketTimeoutMS appropriately in the connection string or client kwargs.

practices.practice: Handle transient faults with retries and exponential backoff; configure driver-level retries where appropriate and implement application-level retry policies with bounded attempts and jitter for idempotent operations.
practices.prior_belief: Enable (or implement) automatic retries with exponential backoff for transient network/availability errors and idempotent operations; prefer using driver-level retryWrites/retryReads where available plus an application-level retry wrapper for non-idempotent operations.

practices.practice: Create indexes on fields used by filters and aggregation group keys (for example an index on supplier_id and a compound index on (supplier_id, status) to accelerate the open-PO-by-supplier aggregation).

practices.practice: Declare unique business-key indexes at deploy-time (not per request); note unique index builds are foreground operations that block writes while building, so manage index creation in a controlled deployment or migration step.
practices.prior_belief: Create a unique index on any business key (e.g. purchase_order_number) at collection creation time to enforce uniqueness and improve lookup performance; do index creation during app startup or a deploy/seed step, not on each request.

practices.practice: Place $match (filters) as early as possible in aggregation pipelines so the engine can use indexes to reduce documents processed, then $group; use projections and $limit downstream and use allowDiskUse in aggregate options when large aggregations require it.
practices.prior_belief: When designing the aggregation pipeline, $match as early as possible (filter first) then $group; use covered projections to return only required fields and use allowDiskUse=true for large aggregations if supported.

practices.prior_belief: Enforce required fields both at the application layer (Pydantic/Beanie validators) and, where possible, with server-side schema validation (MongoDB JSON Schema validator) to protect against accidental writes from other clients.

practices.practice: Avoid relying on multi-document distributed transactions where possible by modeling to reduce cross-document transactions, but note Azure DocumentDB does support multi-document ACID transactions across collections/shards if required.
practices.prior_belief: Avoid multi-document transactions unless necessary; prefer modeling to reduce cross-document transactions, because distributed transactions add latency and complexity and may be limited in managed MongoDB-compatible services.
